draft.title: The Renaissance and the Reformation
card: Renaissance

A period from about the 1300s to the 1600s, starting in Italy. People took a new interest in the learning and art of ancient Greece and Rome. Artists and thinkers also looked more closely at the human world.
Printing
Printing with movable type spread in Europe from the mid 1400s. Books and ideas could be copied faster and cheaper than by hand.
Reformation
In 1517 a German monk, Martin Luther, publicly criticised some practices of the Catholic Church. His ideas spread, and many people left to form new Protestant churches.
The Reformation split the Church in Western Europe into Catholic and Protestant groups. The two movements were different: one was about learning and art, the other about religion.
draft.remember: Renaissance: a revival of ancient learning and art. Reformation: a split in the Church that began in 1517.

a.q: Which event is part of the Reformation?
opts: Martin Luther criticised Church practices in 1517
Italian artists studied the art of ancient Rome
Printers began to produce books with movable type
Scholars in Italy read ancient Greek writings
a.why: The Reformation was a religious movement that began when Luther criticised the Church in 1517. Studying ancient Rome and Greece belongs to the Renaissance, and it is the most tempting wrong choice because it also happened in Europe in the same long period.
a.clue: Which one is about religion and the Church?

b.q: Priya says the Reformation was a revival of interest in ancient Greek and Roman art. What is wrong with her statement?
opts: That describes the Renaissance, not the Reformation
It was a revival of ancient art, but not Roman art
The Reformation took place before the Renaissance
The Reformation was a revival, but only of learning
b.why: A revival of ancient learning and art is the Renaissance. The Reformation was a religious split in the Church in Western Europe. Placing the Reformation as a revival of learning mixes up the two movements.
b.clue: Which movement was about the Church?

a.best: Martin Luther criticised Church practices in 1517

b.best: That describes the Renaissance, not the Reformation

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a precise detail (the date 1517) and the only one naming Luther, so it stands out from the other options. A student could pick it without understanding what the Reformation was.

a.q: Which of these events is part of the Reformation?
opts: German towns set up new Protestant churches
Italian painters copied the styles of Roman art
Scholars in Florence studied ancient Greek books
Architects in Rome built domes like ancient temples
